title: Trump Freezes Bipartisan Russia Sanctions Package, Citing 'National Interest'
snippet: President Donald Trump signed an executive order pausing a sweeping congressional sanctions law targeting Russia just two days before its implementation deadline, sparking intense backlash from lawmakers.
content:
WASHINGTON — President Donald Trump has unexpectedly halted the implementation of a major bipartisan Russia sanctions package, issuing a late-night executive order to freeze the measure under the claim of safeguarding U.S. national interests.

The decision comes just 48 hours before a legally mandated deadline for the sanctions to take effect. Trump had personally signed the bill into law last month following its overwhelming passage in both chambers of Congress, making Friday's sudden reversal a startling pivot that drew immediate condemnation from Capitol Hill.

A Blow to Bipartisan Legislation

The legislation was named in memory of the late Sen. Lindsey Graham (R-S.C.), a fierce advocate for Ukrainian sovereignty who died unexpectedly in July. Crafted alongside Sen. Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.), the package was designed to starve Kremlin forces of critical war funding by penalizing Russian officials, targeting state-backed financial institutions, and cracking down on the shadow fleet of oil tankers keeping Russian energy exports afloat.

The law also authorized Trump to impose tariffs of up to 100% on major importers of Russian oil and gas, with limited exemptions for allies taking active steps to reduce their reliance on Moscow.

Reaction from lawmakers was swift. "These waivers have nothing to do with our national security, and everything to do with sucking up to Vladimir Putin," Blumenthal said in a statement released shortly after the White House announcement.

Energy Deals and Political Pressure

The freeze comes on the heels of another controversial move by the administration. Just last week, Trump announced a deal for the U.S. to purchase over 1.8 million tons of diesel from Russia in a bid to suppress elevated domestic fuel prices. The agreement sparked bipartisan outrage from critics who argued it aids Russia's war effort without mitigating gas price spikes driven primarily by ongoing U.S. military tension with Iran.

The White House submitted a notification to Congress late Friday evening confirming the freeze, though administration officials offered no immediate public details explaining how delaying the sanctions serves American national security.

The political maneuvering comes as the administration faces intense headwinds ahead of the Nov. 3 midterm elections. With public approval numbers dipping over rising consumer costs and foreign policy disputes, Republicans are fighting to preserve their majorities in both the House and Senate.
